assistant|derailleur_tip_limit_screws: Check L and H limit screws so the derailleur neither shifts into the spokes nor blocks shifting
assistant|derailleur_tip_barrel_adjuster: Turn barrel adjuster clockwise to increase cable tension, counterclockwise to decrease; start 1-2 turns clockwise from fully loose
assistant|derailleur_tip_alignment: Ensure derailleur is parallel to cassette and hanger is straight
assistant|derailleur_tip_small_cog: Shift into smallest cog (11/12-tooth) and check derailleur is not rubbing the cassette
assistant|derailleur_tip_large_cog: In largest cog (25/28-tooth) keep about 1-2 mm clearance between derailleur and cassette
assistant|derailleur_tip_chain_length: Check chain length; too long a chain can cause shifting issues
assistant|route_golden_gate_sausalito: Recommends Golden Gate Bridge to Sausalito route with bridge, Alcatraz, and Marin Headlands views
assistant|route_dumbarton_bridge_loop: Recommends 30-mile Dumbarton Bridge Loop through Fremont and Newark back to East Bay
assistant|route_san_mateo_county_coast: Recommends San Mateo County Coast route through Half Moon Bay, Pescadero, and Santa Cruz
assistant|route_mount_tamalpais: Recommends Mount Tamalpais as a challenging climb with Bay Area and Pacific Ocean views
assistant|route_berkeley_hills: Recommends Berkeley Hills scenic loop with views of the Bay
assistant|carbon_wheel_pros: Carbon fiber wheels are lighter, stiffer, more aerodynamic, and absorb road vibrations better
assistant|carbon_wheel_cons: Carbon fiber wheels cost $1,000-$5,000+, are more damage-prone, and may need special brake pads
assistant|carbon_wheel_assessment: Advised that after 2,000 miles current wheels are likely still in good condition; worth upgrading only if experiencing wear or performance issues
assistant|century_readiness_checks: Before a century ride check tires, chain and cassette, brake pads, cables and housing, wheel bearings, frame and fork, saddle and handlebars
assistant|century_ride_tips: Advised gradual training, nutrition/hydration planning, comfortable pacing, and group or support-vehicle riding for a century
assistant|multi_bike_opinion: Advised that three purpose-specific bikes is not too many; benefits include variety, specialization, redundancy, and convenience
assistant|multi_bike_tips: Suggested designating a primary bike, rotating maintenance, keeping a bike journal, and setting a bike budget
assistant|bike_computer_garmin_edge: Recommended Garmin Edge series with GPS, heart rate monitoring, and performance tracking
assistant|bike_computer_wahoo_elemnt: Recommended Wahoo Elemnt series with GPS, heart rate monitoring, and app integration
assistant|bike_computer_lezyne: Recommended Lezyne Super GPS as a compact, affordable device with customizable data screens
assistant|bike_computer_features: Advised considering GPS accuracy, heart rate monitoring, data tracking, customization, app integration, battery life, and water resistance
assistant|phone_mount_options: Suggested phone cases from Lifeproof or Quad Lock, mounts from Quad Lock or Rokform, and weather-resistant pouches from Aquapac or H2O Audio

assistant|road_bike_prep_tires: Check tire pressure and condition, with adequate tread depth and no wear

assistant|road_bike_prep_drivetrain: Clean and lube chain; inspect cassette for wear and replace if near end of lifespan
assistant|road_bike_prep_gears: Ensure derailleurs are properly adjusted and shifting smoothly
assistant|road_bike_prep_bolts: Check all bolts and screws (stem, handlebars, seatpost) are securely tightened
assistant|road_bike_prep_cables: Inspect brake and gear cables for fraying or damage and replace if necessary
assistant|road_bike_prep_comfort: Consider replacing worn saddle and handlebar tape for comfort on long rides
assistant|road_bike_prep_accessories: Ensure bike computer, lights, and accessories are securely attached and functioning

assistant|pre_ride_check_tip: Perform a quick pre-ride check of tire pressure, brakes, and gears before each ride
